Text: The {{c1::JDK}} contains compilation and profiling tools, whereas the {{c2::JRE}} only contains libraries and the JVM launcher.
Extra: The JDK includes `javac` and `jdb`. The JRE is a subset of the JDK designed to run pre-compiled Java programs without development utilities.

Text: The {{c1::JVM}} is the execution engine that translates intermediate bytecode into CPU-specific native machine instructions.
Extra: Bytecode files are stored as `.class` files. The JVM executes them using an interpreter or compiles hot paths using JIT to machine code.

Text: Java is strictly {{c1::pass-by-value}}, meaning it passes copies of references (pointers) rather than variables themselves.
Extra: Passing a copy of the reference pointer allows the method to mutate the object's fields, but reassigning the parameter does not affect the caller's variable.

Text: In Java, the {{c1::==}} operator checks reference or memory address equality, while the {{c2::equals()}} method checks logical value equality.
Extra: By default, `Object.equals()` performs reference identity check. Many classes (like String or Integer) override it to compare field values.

Text: Under the hood, a `HashSet` is backed by a private transient {{c1::HashMap}} instance.
Extra: All elements added to the `HashSet` are stored as keys in this backing map, ensuring uniqueness since map keys cannot contain duplicates.

Text: When you call `hashSet.add(element)`, it internally executes `map.put(element, {{c1::PRESENT}})`.
Extra: `PRESENT` is a static dummy Object used as a constant value for all elements in the backing map.

Text: `HashSet` duplicate checking relies on overriding both the {{c1::hashCode()}} and {{c2::equals()}} methods.
Extra: If they are not overridden, Java will use default Object identity hashing, causing the set to treat duplicate object instances as unique.

Text: The {{c1::Comparable}} interface defines natural ordering inside the entity class, whereas {{c2::Comparator}} defines custom sorting rules externally.
Extra: Comparable requires implementing `compareTo(T o)`, while Comparator requires implementing `compare(T o1, T o2)`.

Text: A method implementing `Comparable.compareTo` must return a negative, zero, or positive integer to represent {{c1::less than::relationship}}, {{c2::equal to}}, or {{c3::greater than}}.
Extra: Returning these sign values allows sorting algorithms (like Timsort) to arrange elements in order.

Text: Stream {{c1::map()}} transforms a stream of elements 1-to-1, while {{c2::flatMap()}} flattens nested streams/collections into a single outer stream.
Extra: Use `map` to change types or extract properties. Use `flatMap` when each input element maps to a collection or stream.

Text: Due to {{c1::type erasure}}, generic type information is stripped out by the compiler, leaving raw bounds in bytecode.
Extra: The JVM only executes raw bytecode and is unaware of the generic arguments, relying on implicit casts inserted during compilation.

Text: When generic compile-time type verification is bypassed, incorrect objects in collections can cause {{c1::Heap Pollution}} and trigger ClassCastException at runtime.
Extra: This occurs when raw types are mixed with generic collections, allowing mismatched objects to be added without compile errors.
